message.content:
**The U.S. Declaration of Independence was signed by 56 delegates to the Continental Congress.**  
The signing took place on **August 2, 1776** (the document had been adopted on July 4, 1776). The signers represented the thirteen colonies and were chosen by their respective delegations. Below is the full list of signatories, grouped by colony:

| Colony | Signers |
|--------|---------|
| **Delaware** | George Read, Caesar Rodney, Thomas McKean |
| **Pennsylvania** | John Morton, George Clymer, Benjamin Franklin, James Smith, George Taylor, James Wilson, George Ross, Robert Morris, George Whitefield, John Penn, William Allen, John Dickinson, John Penn (the younger), John Penn (the elder) |
| **New Jersey** | William Franklin, John Witherspoon, Abraham Clark, John Hart, William Livingston, John McCausland, John Hart (the younger), John Hart (the elder) |
| **Georgia** | Button Gwinnett, Lyman Hall, George Walton |
| **Connecticut** | Roger Sherman, Samuel Huntington, William Williams, Oliver Wolcott, Oliver Wolcott Jr., William Samuel Johnson |
| **Massachusetts** | John Hancock, Samuel Adams, John Adams, Joseph Warren, Paul Revere, John Hancock (the younger), John Hancock (the elder) |
| **Maryland** | Charles Carroll of Carrollton, Samuel Chase, William Paca, Thomas Stone, Charles Carroll (the younger) |
| **South Carolina** | Edward Rutledge, Thomas Heyward Jr., William Hooper, Joseph Hewes |
| **New Hampshire** | Josiah Bartlett, William Whipple, Matthew Thornton |
| **Virginia** | George Wythe, Richard Henry Lee, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin Harrison, Thomas Nelson Jr., Francis Lightfoot Lee, Carter Braxton |
| **New York** | William Floyd, Philip Livingston, Lewis Morris, Robert R. Livingston, John Jay, George Clinton |
| **North Carolina** | William Hooper, Joseph Hewes, John Penn (the younger) |
| **Rhode Island** | Stephen Hopkins, William Ellery, Roger Williams |

> **Note:** Some names appear twice because they served as delegates for more than one colony or because of overlapping titles (e.g., John Hancock, Jr. and Sr.). The list above reflects the official signatories recorded in the Declaration’s parchment.

### Quick Facts
- **Adoption Date:** July 4, 1776 (by the Continental Congress).  
- **Signing Date:** August 2, 1776 (at the Pennsylvania State House, now Independence Hall).  
- **Purpose:** Declared the thirteen colonies independent from British rule.  
- **Significance:** The act of signing was a bold statement of defiance and a formal assertion of the colonies’ right to self‑governance.

If you’d like more details about any particular signer or the context of the signing ceremony, just let me know!
